questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The highest restaurants in the world
What happens to the tips we give in restaurants
How to become a waiter in a good restaurant
Why restaurant food has become so expensive
questions.why: Sam says the programme is about tipping, and asks where that money goes and who receives it.

questions.q: What does Neil say about tipping in the UK?
options: It is against the law in most places
It is only expected in expensive restaurants
It must always be paid in cash
It's a choice, but people usually expect it
questions.why: He says tipping is discretionary, but in most places in the UK it's an expected practice.

questions.q: What do some people wrongly believe about tips?
options: That the person who served them gets the money
That the money goes to the government
That the chef keeps all the money
That tips are added to the price of food
questions.why: Neil says some think the person who brought our food gets the money, 'however that isn't always the case'.

questions.q: What is James James's opinion of restaurant tipping systems?
options: They are all the same and work well
They are fair to kitchen staff only
They differ, but they're all unfair
They are better than they used to be
questions.why: He says there's nothing consistent about them, 'and they're all unfair in their own equal way'.

questions.q: According to James, what do customers tip for?
options: The quality of the food
The service he gives
The price of the meal
The nice restaurant
questions.why: He says he has to earn a tip for the service he provides; 'people don't tip for good food'.

questions.q: What does James's story about the tip jar show?
options: The other servers earned much less than him
Customers had stopped leaving cash tips
The restaurant had lost all the money
He got back far less than he put in
questions.why: He put £50 in the jar in his first week, but at the end of the week he was given £2.45.

questions.q: How does a tronc system work?
options: Tips go into a separate independent bank account
Each waiter keeps the tips from their own tables
Managers decide who gets tips each week
Customers pay their tips directly to the tax office
questions.why: Sam says tips are collected in one separate independent bank account, avoiding the wrong rate of tax.

questions.q: According to Kate Nicholls, why are troncs becoming more important?
options: Because restaurants are paying lower wages
Because customers are leaving bigger tips
More tips are now paid by card, not cash
Because the tax office has changed the rules
questions.why: She says as we move towards a cashless society, more tips are coming through on card payments.
